main_text.l: Credidit è Stygijs umbris se in sidera tolli.

l.i: Tunc Synodus Nicæna fuit celebrata subipso Cæsare, & impietas Arrij damnata, volentis Partiri naturam unam natiq; patriq;.

main_text.l: Cæsar hic in nostram gestars pia pectora gentem, Maxima templa Deo, diuisq; eduxit in auras. Immensas donauit opes, uasa aurea, fundos, Vnde sacerdotes magnis proventibus aucti.

Huius Syluestri permulta struntur instituta de chrismate consecrando, ordinibus dandis, pueris confirmandis, templis prnandis [?], altaribus tegendis, missatoribus constituendis, ungendis, uestiendis [?]: hostijsq; (ut uocant) deificandis, adorandis, feruandis. Item de Dalmaticis, cappis, corporalibus, aliis, mitris, pallijs, pannis, peplis, sindonibus, sacrificijs, cæremonijs, asylis, extremis unctionibus, aliisq; ritibus, non solum Iudaicis, sed & ethnicis, superstitiosis [?], ac diabolicis, ab Apostolo Paulo atq; ipso Christo damnatis.

Dicitur quoq; à Polydoro, Platina, & aliis Romanistarum scriptoribus, ethnicorum dierum nomina, Solis, Lunæ, Martis, Mercurij, Iouis, Veneris, & Saturni, ad Christianorum vsum, in Iudæorum feriis commutasse, ac Phrygiam mitram aurei diadematis loco occupasse. De eius vero mi-

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "gestars" (possibly gestans), "auti" (printed with a long-s form, possibly aucti), "prnandis" (abbreviation unclear, possibly ornandis), "uestiedus" (possibly uestiendis), and "perftitiofis" read as superstitiosis. Long s read as s throughout. Printed "findonibus" and "afylis" read as sindonibus and asylis. The line "uaja" is read as uasa. The opening line is a continuation of verse from the previous page. The last word "raculis" is a catchword, and the text ends with the hyphenated "mi-".
